## Biography

Dr. Patrick F. Suthers is an Assistant Research Professor in the Department of Chemical Engineering at Penn State University. His research focuses on computational systems biology, genome-scale metabolic modeling, metabolic flux analysis, kinetic modeling, and the integration of biological datasets to understand and engineer microbial and plant metabolism.

His work develops and applies mathematical and computational frameworks for analyzing metabolic networks, predicting cellular phenotypes, identifying engineering targets, and improving the biological realism of large-scale models. These approaches support research in biotechnology, sustainable biomanufacturing, bioenergy, and plant systems biology.

## Current Research

Dr. Suthers' research includes:

* Construction and refinement of genome-scale metabolic models
* Constraint-based and kinetic modeling of metabolic networks
* Metabolic flux analysis and atom-mapping methods
* Resource-allocation models for microbial systems
* Computational prediction of metabolic engineering targets
* Modeling plant metabolism and stress responses
* Integration of stoichiometric, thermodynamic, kinetic, and omics data

---

## Software and Computational Methods

Representative areas of software and method development include:

* Genome-scale metabolic reconstruction
* Elementary metabolite unit methods
* Metabolic flux-analysis algorithms
* Large-scale kinetic-model parameterization
* Constraint-based optimization
* Computational frameworks for plant and microbial metabolism

## Collaborations

Dr. Suthers collaborates with the Briseño Lab on systems-level interpretation of host–virus interactions, metabolic consequences of infection, network analysis, and computational integration of virome and host-response datasets.
